Garrett wants the L-4 street tree revision worked into the landscape sheets and the package back to Yeoman for the 11/30 resubmittal. Check it against the current landscape sheets and the resubmittal tracker, then tell me whether we can commit to that date on this revision and what has to happen first. One memo to Callaway for my signature, dated 10/31/2026.

## Where to put your answer

Save the files that make up your answer under `output/` in this workspace,
creating that directory if it does not exist. What gets reviewed when you
finish is `output/`, any file you create or change elsewhere in this
workspace, and your final message. Files you copy into `output/` are read as
part of your answer.

Garrett —

Quick answer on the map runway, since you asked. Under NRS 278.360 the tentative gets four years from approval to run its course. Yours was approved 03/14/2022, so the base clock runs to 03/14/2026 — but the statute also allows a two-year extension on top of that, so effectively you're covered out to 03/14/2028. That's a comfortable window.

Bottom line: you've got plenty of runway on the entitlement side. I wouldn't sweat the December recordation date from a TM standpoint — the tentative is the thing that has to stay alive, and by my read it's alive well into '28. Obviously your land-use counsel is the one to sign off on that, but from where I sit on the title side I'm not seeing any exposure that would make me want to rush anyone.

Order SBT-2026-04188 is ready whenever you are on the escrow side — I've cleared the mechanical items we flagged in July, and Schedule B is in pretty good shape. Happy to walk you and Max through it on a call if that's useful, or we can just proceed to commitment when you give the word.

Ping me if you want to talk it through.

 Recital of the Request

Enterprise Town Advisory Board, the Planning Commission finds that:
The tentative map substantially conforms to the requirements of Chapter 30 of the Clark County Code (Title
30 — Unified Development Code) applicable to the property, subject to the conditions of approval set forth
herein.
The proposed subdivision is consistent with the goals and objectives of the adopted Enterprise Land Use
Plan and the Clark County Comprehensive Master Plan.

conditions herein.

including but not limited to NRS 278.360, quoted below.

 Statutory Presentation Requirements

subdivision, the substance of which is summarised below:

governing body within four (4) years after the date of approval or conditional approval of the tentative
map. Each successive final map in the same series must be presented within two (2) years after the

application filed after the applicable period has expired, grant an extension of not more than two (2)

governing body. Nothing in this letter, and no informal communication from staff, shall be construed to extend,

knuckles, and turning radii shall satisfy the requirements of both Public Works and the Clark County Fire
Department.
Sight visibility triangles shall be shown on the improvement plans and the landscape plans at every
intersection and driveway. Landscaping, signage, and walls within the sight visibility zone shall comply with
Section 30.52.025 (Sight Zones) of the Clark County Code.

Dear Mr. Nokes:
Comprehensive Planning is in receipt of the written application submitted by Callaway Land Partners on
October 28, 2024, requesting an Extension of Time in which to present the first final map in the series under
TM-22-500041. This letter is the Department's response and, together with your application, constitutes the
official record for the tentative map file with respect to the extension question and the subsequent map clock.

--- Page 3 ---
1. Governing statute — NRS 278.360
The extension mechanism available under Nevada law is set forth in NRS 278.360. In pertinent part, the statute
provides:
"The governing body may, upon written application filed after the applicable period has expired,
grant an extension of not more than two (2) years. An extension shall not be granted before the
applicable presentation period has expired."
The statute is written in mandatory terms and its two operative preconditions — a written application, and a filing
date after the applicable period has expired — are jurisdictional. The County has no discretion to relax them.
 2. Disposition of the 10/28/2024 application
Because the Callaway Land Partners application of 10/28/2024 was filed before the applicable presentation
period had expired, the County is without authority to act on it on the merits. The application is not properly
before the County until the applicable period has expired, and the County therefore declines to act on the
request in advance of the presentation period. This is a jurisdictional disposition, not a rejection on the merits.
Nothing in this letter forecloses any future written application filed by Callaway Land Partners in compliance with
the statutory precondition, if and when the applicable period has expired and Callaway has cause to seek relief.
Any such future application would be evaluated on its own record and on the standards then applicable.
 3. Presentation of the first final map in the series
The Department has been advised, and the Clark County Recorder's index confirms, that the first final map in
the series under TM-22-500041 — Desert Sage Ranch Phases 1 & 2 (100 residential lots on approximately 100
acres, together with a remainder parcel for future Phase 3) — has been presented and recorded of record. The
applicant may consult the Recorder's public index for the recording particulars.
The four-year first-map presentation clock that runs from the date of tentative map approval has accordingly
been satisfied and is no longer at issue with respect to Desert Sage Ranch.
 4. Presentation clock for successive final maps
The applicable statutory framework under NRS 278.360 continues to govern the tentative map. The applicant
and its design consultants are directed to confirm the operative presentation deadline for any successive map
with Comprehensive Planning. Failure to timely present a successive map within the applicable statutory period
would terminate all further proceedings under TM-22-500041.
 5. Notes for the file
 No fee refund is issued; the application fee submitted with the 10/28/2024 filing has been retained per the
Department's fee schedule for processing of the written record and this response.
 This letter has been indexed to the TM-22-500041 file and copied to Public Works Development Review
for coordination with any Phase 3 improvement plan and final map application that may be submitted in due
course.

undersigned in writing so that the response may be added to the same file.

accordance with the District’s Service Rules then in force.

conveyance of onsite mains to the District upon acceptance.

 hydrants, service laterals, and appurtenances in strict conformance with the District’s current Design and
Construction Standards. Improvement plans must be submitted to the District’s Engineering Services group for
review and approval prior to construction; District field inspection is required through acceptance.

 Plumbing Code, the Nevada Administrative Code, and the District’s Cross-Connection Control Program, including

approved by the University of Southern California Foundation for Cross-Connection Control and Hydraulic
Research and shall be tested by a certified tester on the schedule required by the District.

Submitting an Application for TAB Recommendation
Any application requiring a recommendation of the Enterprise Town Advisory Board — including variance
applications, use permits, waivers, design review items, and zone changes — must be filed with Clark County
Comprehensive Planning and referred to the TAB by staff. To appear on a given meeting agenda, the complete

Comprehensive Planning no later than 21 days prior to the meeting date. This period is necessary to permit staff

Compliance Bulletin and Functional Turf Definitions
Bulletin No.

Compliance
Deadline
12/31/2026
Applies To
All properties within the SNWA service area other than individually-owned single-family
residential lots
1. Purpose
This bulletin implements the nonfunctional turf prohibition enacted by the Nevada Legislature in Assembly Bill
356 (2021) and administered within the SNWA service area by the Southern Nevada Water Authority in
cooperation with its member agencies. Assembly Bill 356 directs the removal of nonfunctional turf from
properties served by the Colorado River Commission of Nevada and, by extension, from properties served by
SNWA member agencies.
The compliance deadline for the removal or conversion of all nonfunctional turf on properties subject to the
prohibition is 12/31/2026. On and after that date, the presence of nonfunctional turf on a property subject to the
prohibition constitutes a continuing violation of the state statute and of the water service rules of the SNWA
member agencies.
The prohibition applies to, without limitation:

Homeowner association (HOA) owned or managed common-area property, including entry features,
streetscape strips, medians, park parcels, tot lots, and greenbelts;

Commercial, industrial, mixed-use, institutional, and multi-family residential properties;

Governmental, quasi-governmental, and school-district properties;

Vacant parcels held for future development on which existing turf remains irrigated.
Property owners and their agents are directed to identify all turf areas on affected properties, to classify each
area as functional or nonfunctional under the definitions set out in Section 3, and to schedule conversion of
nonfunctional areas so that removal is complete on or before the deadline.
2. Single-Family Residential Carve-Out
The nonfunctional turf prohibition does not apply to turf located within an individually-owned single-family
residential lot. Turf inside the recorded boundary of a single-family residential lot — front yard, side yard, back
yard, and any other area within the four corners of the lot as recorded — is exempt from the mandate
established by AB 356 and this bulletin. Owners of single-family residential lots remain subject to the general
water-waste ordinances and outdoor-watering restrictions of their retail purveyor but are not required by AB
356 to remove existing turf.
The single-family residential carve-out is lot-based, not project-based. The following areas are outside the
carve-out and remain fully subject to the prohibition even where they lie within a subdivision the zoning of

--- Page 2 ---
SNWA
SOUTHERN NEVADA WATER AUTHORITY
Water Resources & Conservation Division
100 City Parkway, Suite 700  ·  Las Vegas, NV 89106
Southern Nevada Water Authority  |  Nonfunctional Turf Prohibition — Compliance Bulletin  |  WRC-2024-07
Page 2
Issued in cooperation with SNWA member agencies · Not a modification of statute or member-agency service rules.
which is single-family residential:

HOA-owned or HOA-managed common-area parcels of any description, including but not limited to park
parcels, tot lots, greenbelts, drainage tracts, entry features, monument islands, and landscape maintenance
strips;

Streetscape and parkway areas between the back of curb and the right-of-way line, or between the
right-of-way line and the lot line, where those areas are owned or maintained by the HOA, a landscape
maintenance district, or a public agency;

Detention/retention basin floors and slopes;

Any parcel held in common ownership by two or more lot owners through a homeowner association or
similar body.
A property is within the carve-out only where the turf in question lies inside the recorded boundary of an
individually-owned single-family residential lot. Turf lying outside those boundaries — even by inches, and
even where the adjacent lot owner mows it — is not within the carve-out. Developers, landscape architects, and
HOA managers are cautioned that the presence of a single-family residential zoning designation on the
underlying parcel does not confer the carve-out on common-area turf within that parcel; the operative
distinction is the lot line, not the zoning district.
3. Functional Turf Categories
Turf that lies outside the single-family residential carve-out is subject to the prohibition unless it qualifies under
one of the functional categories set out below. Each category has a specific qualifying test. Turf that does not
satisfy the test for one of these categories is nonfunctional turf and must be converted on or before the deadline.
3.1 Playground Turf
Definition. Grass located within a designated play area containing playground amenities including slides,
swings, and climbing structures, on homeowner association owned or managed common-area property.
Qualifying test. All of the following must be present:
1.
The turf lies within a designated play area — that is, an area drawn on approved landscape plans, or
established on the ground by fencing, borders, or other physical delineation, and identified as a play area
intended for use by children.
2.
The designated play area contains installed and operable playground amenities of the character enumerated
above — specifically, slides, swings, and climbing structures. A designated play area lacking installed
playground amenities does not qualify as playground turf, regardless of the sign or plan label attached to
the area.
3.
The turf lies on property owned or managed by a homeowner association, or by a comparable body
responsible for the common-area landscape.
Turf lying outside the boundary of the designated play area — even in the same park parcel, and even if
visually continuous with the qualifying turf — does not fall within this category and must be classified
independently.

--- Page 3 ---

Water Resources & Conservation Division
100 City Parkway, Suite 700  ·  Las Vegas, NV 89106
Southern Nevada Water Authority  |  Nonfunctional Turf Prohibition — Compliance Bulletin  |  WRC-2024-07
Page 3
Issued in cooperation with SNWA member agencies · Not a modification of statute or member-agency service rules.
Figure 1 — Playground Turf, Schematic. A common-area park parcel is shown in plan view. Within the
parcel, a rectangular sub-area is bordered and labeled “designated play area.” Inside that sub-area are three
symbols: a slide, a swing set, and a climbing structure. Turf inside the bordered sub-area is shaded and marked
“functional (playground).” Turf in the balance of the parcel, outside the border, is shaded a different color and
marked “nonfunctional unless another category applies.”
Qualifying test is satisfied by the turf shown inside the bordered sub-area only.
3.2 Athletic Field Turf
Definition. A contiguous turf area of not less than 1,500 contiguous square feet with no dimension less than
30 feet, used for organized athletic activity.
Qualifying test. All of the following must be present:
1.
The turf area is contiguous — i.e., forming a single, connected surface uninterrupted by pavement, planter,
structure, or non-turf ground cover — and measures at least 1,500 square feet in aggregate area.
2.
The shortest dimension of that contiguous area, measured perpendicular to its longest dimension, is not
less than 30 feet.
3.
The area is used, or is dedicated to be used, for organized athletic activity — organized team sports,
physical education, formal recreation league play, or similar use. General passive lawn use, decorative
lawn, and informal recreation do not satisfy this element.
A grass area meeting the geometric thresholds but lacking a documented athletic use does not qualify.
Conversely, a grass area used for organized athletic activity that fails either the 1,500-square-foot minimum or
the 30-foot minimum dimension does not qualify.
Figure 2 — Athletic Field Turf, Geometric Thresholds. Three plan-view rectangles are compared side by
side. Rectangle A measures 60 feet by 40 feet (2,400 sf) — labeled “qualifies: exceeds 1,500 sf minimum and
30 ft minimum dimension.” Rectangle B measures 100 feet by 20 feet (2,000 sf) — labeled “does not qualify:
fails 30 ft minimum dimension notwithstanding total area.” Rectangle C measures 40 feet by 30 feet (1,200 sf)
— labeled “does not qualify: fails 1,500 sf minimum notwithstanding 30 ft dimension.”
Both thresholds must be met by the same contiguous area.
3.3 Pet Relief Turf (Limited)
Turf provided as a pet-relief area on multi-family residential, hotel, or comparable properties may qualify as
functional in limited circumstances. Where allowed, pet-relief turf is capped at a modest area per property, must
be enclosed, must be identified by signage, and must be reasonably necessary in light of the character of the
property served. Pet-relief turf on HOA common area serving single-family residential subdivisions is generally
not recognized under this category and should not be relied on to justify continued irrigation of common-area
lawn.
3.4 Special-Use Turf by Application
Turf that serves a demonstrable functional purpose not captured by the categories above — for example,
cemetery lawn, historic-district lawn, or grass specified by an accessibility program — may be recognized as

Project Description

--- Page 2 ---
Landscape improvements for Phase 3 of the Desert Sage Ranch subdivision: 40.0 acres, 60 half-acre
single-family residential lots. Work includes street frontage landscape strips along the extended Windmill Ln.
frontage and the Phase 3 interior collector, the Phase 3 entry monument at the intersection of Rainbow Blvd.
and the interior collector, and the HOA common-area park at Parcel A (identified as Common-Area Parcel "D"
on the Phase 3 civil improvement plans; the two designations refer to the same physical parcel). Turf is provided
only within the HOA common-area park at Parcel A. No turf is proposed in any streetscape, median, entry
treatment, or any location within ten feet of a street or curb. The park turf species is a cool-season Kentucky
bluegrass / perennial ryegrass blend selected for the Phase 3 park lawn program; the desert planting palette and
streetscape treatments extend the palette established for Phases 1 & 2.
General Landscape Notes
1.  All work shall conform to Clark County Code Title 30, Chapter 30.64 (Landscaping, Walls and Buffers), the
Southern Nevada Regional Plant List, and the Clark County Standard Drawings current at the date of
submittal.
2.  Turf placement complies with Clark County Code sec. 30.64.030(j), which permits turf in conjunction with
cemeteries, parks and schools and prohibits turf within ten feet of a street or curb. The restrictions of sec.
30.64.030(j) may not be waived or varied and have been observed throughout Phase 3.
3.  Turf within Phase 3 is provided only within the HOA common-area park at Parcel A, as detailed on Sheet
L-3. Turf is not provided in any streetscape, median, entry treatment, or lot.
4.  Streetscape planting is limited to drip-irrigated, desert-adapted species listed on the Southern Nevada
Regional Plant List, consistent with the palette approved for Phases 1 & 2.
5.  All planted areas shall be irrigated by an automatic controller with rain-sensor and freeze-sensor lockout.
6.  Turf areas shall be spray-irrigated on a dedicated station; all other planted areas shall be drip-irrigated on
separate stations.
7.  Street tree spacing shall meet the Clark County canopy standard of one tree per twenty linear feet of
dedicated street frontage, measured continuously along each dedicated right-of-way. Refer to Sheet L-2 for
streetscape layout and plant schedule below for tree counts as shown.
8.  Minimum tree size at installation: 24-inch box, single-trunk unless noted, with a minimum caliper of 1.5
inches measured six inches above finish grade.
9.  Planting pits shall be excavated to twice the width and one-and-one-half times the depth of the root ball.
Backfill shall be native soil amended with organic material at a rate of one part amendment to three parts
native soil.
10.  A three-inch layer of decomposed granite mulch (¾-inch minus, tan) shall be provided over all planted areas
outside the common-area park turf area. Wood or bark mulches are not permitted.
11.  All landscape shall be maintained by the Desert Sage Ranch HOA under the CC&Rs. Common-area
maintenance boundaries are shown on the CC&R common-area exhibit and are not repeated on these
sheets.
12.  Contractor shall verify all existing utility locations prior to excavation and shall not plant trees within any
dedicated utility easement without written permission of the utility.

1.  Attendees
Distribution of these notes: attendees above, plus CCFD Fire Plans Examiner (Capt. Emmett Roark) and Sundial project file 2201-03.
2.  County Submittal and Inspection Sequence
The construction inspection sequence was walked through by Terrence Kolb (Clark County Public Works — Development Review). The following items were agreed and will govern Phase 2 inspection administration:
2.1  Inspection request procedure.
Mesquite Basin will submit inspection requests through the County Public Works construction inspection portal not less than 48 hours in advance of the requested inspection window. Requests will cite the improvement plan sheet, station range, and item to be inspected. Sundial's field engineer will be copied on each request; where the field engineer's presence is required (e.g., subgrade acceptance, storm drain pressure test, pavement structural section) Sundial will attend jointly with the County inspector.
2.2  Progressive inspections during construction.
Phase 2 will be inspected on a rolling basis by item: rough grading and moisture-density; storm drain trench, bedding and pressure tests prior to backfill; curb-and-gutter forming; subbase; base; and pavement placement. County inspector will sign each item on County inspection form; Sundial will maintain the running set of signed reports in the construction record for Phase 2.
2.3  Pre-final inspection.
When the improvements listed on the approved plans are complete in the field — including punch-list-condition landscape, signing and striping, and the temporary construction stub at the north boundary as shown on the improvement plans — Callaway will submit a written request for pre-final inspection. County will schedule the pre-final walk within ten (10) working days of the request. Sundial and Mesquite Basin will attend. Any punch items identified will be logged on the County form on-site and returned to Callaway the same week.
2.4  Final inspection and acceptance.
Following completion of pre-final punch, Callaway will submit a written request for final inspection with a signed contractor statement that punch items are complete. County will schedule final inspection within ten (10) working days. On satisfactory final inspection, County Public Works will issue a written improvement acceptance letter under separate cover. It was noted that Phase 2 offsite improvements (Rainbow Blvd. frontage, curb return at Windmill Ln., traffic control device) may be finalled and accepted on a schedule independent of the onsite balance; the two acceptances will be handled as separate letters. This is consistent with the release provisions in the Phase 2 improvement agreement and performance bond.
2.5  Record drawings.
Sundial will prepare Phase 2 record drawings (as-builts) from contractor red-lines, field survey, and County inspection reports, for submission with the improvement acceptance package. Sundial will maintain a working red-line set at the trailer for the duration of construction; the general contractor will keep a mirrored set. Record drawings will be sealed and dated after final inspection.
3.  Traffic Control and Access
3.1  Construction access — primary.
Primary construction ingress and egress for Phase 2 will be from Rainbow Blvd. at the approved Phase 2 entry throat. All haul routes into and out of the site will use this entry. A traffic control plan conforming to the MUTCD and Clark County Public Works standards has been submitted by Mesquite Basin and approved for the Rainbow Blvd. work zone (curb return, taper, and flagger station).
3.2  Temporary construction stub across undeveloped Phase 3.
A temporary construction stub will be graded and paved across the northern boundary of the built Phase 2 area, extending into and across the presently undeveloped Phase 3 parcel to tie back to Windmill Ln. This stub is called out on the approved improvement plans and shown on the traffic control exhibit distributed at the meeting.
Two uses of the stub were confirmed and agreed:
Construction traffic.  The stub will serve as a secondary construction access for material deliveries and heavy equipment during Phase 2 construction, relieving the Rainbow Blvd. entry.
Secondary emergency access for occupied Phase 2.  Once dwelling units in Phase 2 are occupied and while Phase 3 remains undeveloped ground, the stub will serve as the secondary point of access required by CCFD for Phase 2 emergency response.
Both uses are expressly temporary. The stub crosses ground that is planned for Phase 3 subdivision development. It exists only because the Phase 3 remainder is presently ungraded and open. When Phase 3 is developed the stub will be removed and superseded by whatever access configuration is approved for Phase 3 on its own merits. This limitation was discussed in the meeting and was subsequently confirmed in writing by CCFD.
CCFD approval status.
At the time of the meeting, the CCFD access approval for Phase 2 was under review. Following the meeting, CCFD issued its formal approval by letter dated 06/12/2023 (Capt. Emmett Roark, Fire Plans Examiner). The letter approves the secondary access configuration for Phase 2 as a temporary condition pending development of Phase 3. That temporary designation is acknowledged on the record. Callaway and Sundial will maintain the CCFD letter in the project record and will treat the stub as a Phase 2 arrangement only; nothing in the CCFD Phase 2 correspondence is to be read as approval of an access configuration for Phase 3.
3.3  Stub construction and maintenance.
Mesquite Basin will construct the stub to the section and alignment shown on the approved Phase 2 improvement plans (compacted aggregate base with a bituminous surface course of the section noted on Sheet C-6). The stub will be barricaded at the Phase 3-side terminus with a Type III barricade and CCFD-compliant emergency-access knock-down gate. The stub will be maintained by Callaway for the duration of Phase 2 occupancy and until Phase 3 construction commences. Weekly inspection of the stub surface and barricade will be logged by Mesquite Basin during construction and by Callaway/HOA thereafter.
3.4  Signage.
"Emergency Access Only — No Public Through-Access" signage will be posted at the stub in both directions, per CCFD sign schedule. Contractor construction-access signage will be posted separately during the construction period only.
4.  BMP Installation Sequence per SWPPP
The project Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP), as authored by Sundial and covered under the NDEP General Permit NVR100000 Notice of Intent for Desert Sage Ranch, governs installation and sequencing of construction stormwater BMPs. The following sequence was walked and agreed on-site:
4.1  Prior to any grading disturbance.
The following perimeter and inlet-protection BMPs will be installed and inspected before any Phase 2 earthwork begins:
Silt fence and reinforced silt fence along the downgradient (south and west) perimeter of the Phase 2 disturbance area, as shown on the SWPPP site map.
Stabilized construction entrance (rock pad with wheel-wash provision) at the Rainbow Blvd. primary construction entry.
Stabilized construction entrance (rock pad) at the temporary stub terminus at Windmill Ln.
Inlet protection (sandbag berm or filter insert) at all existing off-site catch basins within 100 ft of the disturbance boundary along Rainbow Blvd. and Windmill Ln.
Concrete washout containment at the location shown on the SWPPP site map, off the primary construction entry.
Sundial's field engineer will walk the perimeter BMPs with Mesquite Basin's superintendent and sign the SWPPP inspection log the day the perimeter is complete and before earthwork disturbance begins.
4.2  During mass grading.
Track-out control at both construction entries will be inspected daily by Mesquite Basin and after each significant rainfall event. Wind-erosion control (application of water and, where directed, tackifier) will follow the schedule in the SWPPP and the requirements of the Clark County Department of Environment and Sustainability dust control permit for the site.
4.3  As storm drain becomes operational.
As Phase 2 catch basins are installed, inlet protection (gravel bag or filter fabric type as noted in the SWPPP) will be placed at each basin the same day the frame and grate are set. Protection will remain in place until final stabilization or until paving is complete, whichever is later.
4.4  Stabilization.
Temporary stabilization of disturbed areas that will remain inactive for more than fourteen (14) days will be by application of tackifier or hydromulch, per the SWPPP. Final stabilization will be by landscape installation in improved areas and by soil binder / gravel treatment on Phase-2-facing slopes of the Phase 3 remainder that are disturbed by grading of the temporary stub.
4.5  Inspections and records.
Mesquite Basin will conduct SWPPP inspections weekly and within 24 hours after any rainfall of 0.25 inch or greater, log each inspection on the SWPPP inspection form, and correct deficiencies within the timeframes specified in the SWPPP. Sundial will spot-audit inspections at not less than a monthly interval. All SWPPP records will be kept at the site trailer and available for review by NDEP or Clark County inspectors.
4.6  Notice of Termination.
When Phase 2 improvements reach final stabilization and the improvements are accepted, Sundial will prepare and file a Notice of Termination with NDEP under NVR100000 to close construction stormwater coverage for the Phase 2 area of disturbance. The Notice of Termination will be limited to the Phase 2 area of disturbance and will be filed in the project record.
5.  Utility Coordination
5.1  Wet utilities.
Water.  Water main installation is by Mesquite Basin under LVVWD standard specifications, on the alignments and to the sizes shown on the approved plans. Pressure test and disinfection to LVVWD standards; LVVWD field acceptance required prior to service connection. LVVWD inspector to be scheduled by Mesquite Basin through the LVVWD construction desk with 48-hour notice.
Sewer.  Sewer main installation is by Mesquite Basin under CCWRD standard specifications. Mandrel test and low-pressure air test on completed reaches; CCWRD field acceptance required prior to backfill approval. Manhole vacuum test on all manholes. CCWRD inspection scheduled through CCWRD Plan Review Engineer's office (Vince Alarid, CCWRD).
5.2  Dry utilities (joint trench).
Composite dry utility plan (electric — NV Energy; gas — Southwest Gas; telecom — CenturyLink and Cox) is on file. Joint trench and conduit installation to be sequenced by Mesquite Basin after storm drain and sewer are backfilled and prior to base course. Each dry utility purveyor will inspect its own facilities prior to trench closure. The dry utility coordinator will attend a joint trench pre-installation meeting on-site before joint trench work begins; date to be set by Mesquite Basin.
5.3  Locating existing.
Blue-stake / USA North 811 will be called by Mesquite Basin for each work area 48 hours in advance of digging. Sundial will provide the contractor with the survey-verified locations of the offsite tie-ins at Rainbow Blvd.
5.4  Utility crossing conflicts.
Any utility crossing conflict identified in the field will be reported by Mesquite Basin to Sundial the same day. Sundial will provide a resolution or field revision within 24 hours where possible; where a field revision affects an approved plan sheet, Sundial will issue a numbered field revision memo and copy the County construction inspector.
5.5  Fire protection features.
Hydrant locations and fire department connections were walked by CCFD (Insp. Voight). Hydrant spacing on the plans meets CCFD standard. Hydrants are to be operational (flushed, tested, and flowed) prior to combustible construction commencing above the foundation on any dwelling unit. Hydrant flow test to be witnessed by CCFD and coordinated by Callaway's builder.
6.  Action Items Carried into Construction

time to time.
Section 2.2. "Association." Desert Sage Ranch Community Association, a Nevada nonprofit corporation,
being the community association formed by Declarant to administer, own, and maintain the Common Area and
to enforce the terms of this Declaration. The Association is the community association contemplated by NRS
Chapter 116. All references herein to "HOA" mean the Association.
Section 2.3. "Board." The Board of Directors of the Association.
Section 2.4. "Bylaws." The Bylaws of the Association, as the same may be amended from time to time.
Section 2.5. "Common Area." All real property (including any Improvements thereon) that is (i) owned by the
Association in fee simple, or (ii) held by the Association under an easement, license, or maintenance obligation
for the common use and enjoyment of the Owners. Common Area expressly includes, without limitation, the
Common-Area Park, the Streetscape Common Area, the Entry Feature, and all landscaping, irrigation
infrastructure, hardscape, walls, monumentation, signage, and amenities located therein as installed by
Declarant or its successors. Common Area does not include any Lot or any portion of a public right-of-way
conveyed by dedication to Clark County or another public body.
Section 2.6. "Common-Area Park." The parcel of Common Area designated on the recorded final map as
Parcel A, being an active-use park parcel improved with landscaping, irrigation, and, as installed by Declarant,
any turf area and any playground amenities (which, where installed, may consist of slides, swings, and climbing
structures). Parcel A is owned by the Association and is not part of any Lot.
Section 2.7. "Declarant." Callaway Land Partners, a Nevada limited liability company, and its successors and
assigns to whom the rights of Declarant hereunder are expressly assigned in a recorded instrument.
Section 2.8. "Declaration." This Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Desert Sage
Ranch, together with all exhibits and attachments hereto and all amendments and supplements duly recorded.

--- Page 3 ---
Section 2.9. "Entry Feature." The parcel of Common Area designated on the recorded final map as Parcel C,
being the community entry treatment situated at the intersection of Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, and
improved with entry monumentation, signage, walls, planting, irrigation, and accent lighting. Parcel C is owned
by the Association and is not part of any Lot.
Section 2.10. "Governing Documents." This Declaration, the Articles, the Bylaws, and the rules and
regulations of the Association, each as the same may be amended from time to time, together with all recorded
exhibits, plats, and supplemental declarations.
Section 2.11. "Improvement." Any structure, wall, fence, monument, sign, tree, shrub, turf, planting, irrigation
line, playground amenity, path, hardscape, or other tangible thing installed upon or affixed to the land.
Section 2.12. "Lot." Each numbered residential lot depicted upon a recorded final map of the Property and
intended for the construction and occupancy of a single detached residential dwelling. Each Lot is a separately
conveyable parcel; no Lot includes any portion of any Common Area, and no Common Area is any part of any
Lot.
Section 2.13. "Managing Agent." The community management firm engaged by the Association pursuant to a
written management agreement to perform the day-to-day administration of the Association's affairs, including
the maintenance and replacement obligations set forth in Article V. As of the date of this Declaration, the
Managing Agent is Sagebrook Community Management LLC, a Nevada limited-liability company, having offices
at 6280 S. Pecos Road, Suite 300, Las Vegas, NV 89120.
Section 2.14. "Map" or "Final Map." Any final subdivision map of any portion of the Property recorded in the
Office of the Clark County Recorder, including the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, recorded at Book
175, Page 60) and any successive final map for Phase 3.
Section 2.15. "Owner." The record holder of fee simple title to a Lot, excluding any person or entity holding title
solely as security for the performance of an obligation.
Section 2.16. "Property." All of the real property described in Article III below and shown upon the Map(s),
together with all Improvements thereon, and any additional property annexed hereto in accordance with this
Declaration.

back-of-curb of a public street and the front or side lot lines of the adjoining Lots (or, where applicable, between
the back-of-curb and a perimeter community wall), extending along all frontage of the Property, and improved
with sidewalks (where the sidewalk is not within the dedicated public right-of-way), desert planting, street trees,
and drip irrigation. Each Streetscape Common Area parcel is owned by the Association and is not part of any
Lot.

property situated in the unincorporated area of Clark County, State of Nevada, more particularly described as
follows:
A portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., Clark County, Nevada,
containing approximately 140.0 acres, together with all easements, tenements, hereditaments, and
appurtenances thereunto belonging, commonly known as Desert Sage Ranch, situated at the
intersection of Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, Las Vegas, Nevada 89178.

--- Page 4 ---

(a) Phase 1 — as more particularly depicted upon the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, Book 175, Page
60), consisting of residential Lots, streetscape and open-space Common Area, and dedicated street
rights-of-way, all as shown upon Sheets 2 through 4 of the First Final Map.

60), consisting of residential Lots, streetscape and open-space Common Area (including the Common-Area
Park designated Parcel A, the shared Detention Facility designated Parcel B, and the Entry Feature designated
Parcel C), and dedicated street rights-of-way, all as shown upon Sheets 2 through 4 of the First Final Map.

County Assessor's Parcel Number 177-27-201-001, to be subdivided into approximately sixty (60) half-acre

depicted upon a successive final map to be recorded by Declarant. Upon recordation of the Phase 3 final map,
the Lots and Common Area created thereby shall automatically be and become subject to this Declaration
without the necessity of any further instrument.
Section 3.3. Annexation of Successive Phases. Declarant reserves the right, exercisable in its sole discretion

Office of the Clark County Recorder that (i) identifies the annexed property by reference to the recorded final
map, and (ii) states that the annexed property is thereby made subject to this Declaration.
Section 3.4. Public Rights-of-Way. All streets, alleys, and other public rights-of-way depicted upon any Map

Area, and the Association bears no maintenance obligation for improvements accepted for public maintenance
within any such dedicated area, except as provided by written agreement with the applicable public body.
 ARTICLE IV. COMMON AREAS
Section 4.1. Establishment of Common Area. Declarant hereby establishes and dedicates for the common
use and enjoyment of the Owners, and conveys to the Association concurrently herewith and by the recordation
of each applicable Map, all Common Area, in fee simple, free and clear of all monetary encumbrances other
than the lien of current taxes and assessments not yet delinquent and matters of record specifically noted upon
the Map.

reflected in Exhibit B hereto) is hereby established as the Common-Area Park. Parcel A is owned in fee simple
by the Association and is not part of any Lot. Parcel A is improved by Declarant with landscaping, irrigation, and,
as installed by Declarant, any turf area and any playground amenities (which, where installed by Declarant, may
consist of slides, swings, and climbing structures). All landscaping, irrigation infrastructure, turf, planting,
hardscape, and playground amenities installed upon Parcel A, as and where installed, constitute Common Area
Improvements owned by the Association.

reflected in Exhibit B hereto) is hereby established as the Entry Feature. Parcel C is owned in fee simple by the

community identification signage, decorative perimeter walls, drip-irrigated desert planting, and accent lighting.

the entire street frontage of the Property, in the extent depicted upon the First Final Map and upon any
successive final map recorded for Phase 3.
Section 4.5. Distinct from Lots. The Common-Area Park (Parcel A), the shared Detention Facility (Parcel B),

maintained by the Association, and no such parcel is a Lot or any part of a Lot. No Owner has any right, by
virtue of ownership of a Lot, to construct, remove, alter, replace, or reconfigure any Improvement located within
any Common Area.
Section 4.6. Easements Appurtenant. Every Owner shall have a nonexclusive easement of use and
enjoyment in and to the Common Area, appurtenant to and passing with title to such Owner's Lot, subject to the

Area Improvements, including without limitation landscaping, irrigation infrastructure, turf, planting, and

Owner may hold at law or in equity.
 ARTICLE V. MAINTENANCE AND REPLACEMENT

MAP AMENDMENT AND VACATION PROCEDURES
Amended Final Maps  ·  Vacation and Abandonment  ·  Realignment within Project Design
At a glance. A recorded final map is a public record. The dedications, easements, and property lines
shown on it may only be modified through one of three routes: Amended Final Map, Vacation and
Abandonment, or an internal Realignment that does not touch a recorded right. Choose the correct route
at the start of the project to avoid duplicate submittals and lost recordation dates.
1.   PURPOSE
This handout summarizes the routes available in Clark County for altering rights, easements, dedications, boundary
lines, lot configurations, or other features that appear on a subdivision map already recorded with the Clark County
Recorder. It is issued jointly by the Clark County Department of Public Works (Development Review and the Office
of the County Surveyor) and the Clark County Department of Comprehensive Planning as evergreen guidance for
owners, engineers, surveyors, and their counsel.
A recorded final map is a public record. The dedications, easements, and property lines shown on it may only be
modified through one of the procedures below. Choosing the correct route at the start of a project avoids duplicate
submittals, wasted review cycles, and lost recordation dates.
The three routes are:
  Amended Final Map — for corrections and modifications that keep the subdivision in place but revise
recorded easements, lot lines, or map features. Utility rights are relinquished and re-granted on the amended plat
itself.
 Vacation and Abandonment — for the elimination of previously dedicated public rights (streets, alleys,
drainage easements, or portions thereof). The action is legislative and requires public hearings.
 Realignment within the applicant's own project design — an in-house design change that does not touch any
recorded right or dedication. No County land action is required, but revised plan sheets and an additional plan
check cycle are.
Applicants unsure which route applies should schedule a pre-application conference with the Office of the County
Surveyor before preparing exhibits.
2.   AMENDED FINAL MAP
An Amended Final Map is used to revise a recorded final map without extinguishing the underlying subdivision.
Typical uses include:
  Correcting scrivener's errors or bearing/distance ties disclosed after recordation.
 Adjusting interior lot lines between adjoining lots under common ownership.
 Relocating, widening, narrowing, or vacating and re-granting private utility easements.
 Adding easements not shown on the original recorded map (for example, a public utility easement needed to
serve a later phase).

--- Page 2 ---
Map Amendment and Vacation Procedures

 Modifying private street or common-area boundaries within the subdivision.
The Amended Final Map is prepared on the Clark County Amended Final Map form. Applicants must use the
current form; earlier versions will be rejected at intake.
2.1 Form Layout and Key Characteristics
(a) Certificate sheet. The certificate sheet of the Amended Final Map reproduces the entire certificate set from the
original recorded map — Owner's Certificate and Dedication, Nevada notary acknowledgment, Utility/Agency
Approvals, Surveyor's Certificate, County Surveyor's Certificate, Zoning Approval, Division of Water Resources
approval, and Southern Nevada Health District certificate — updated for the current signatories, together with an
additional OWNER'S CERTIFICATE OF AMENDMENT executed by the current fee owner(s). The Certificate
of Amendment recites the recording reference (book and page) of the map being amended and identifies, by short
description, what is being changed on each affected sheet.
(b) Utility Relinquishment Block. A dedicated utility relinquishment block is provided on the amended final map
form. In this block the named utility companies whose easements appear on the recorded plats being amended
formally relinquish their rights in those easements in favor of the easements granted (or re-granted) on the new
amended plat. Each named utility executes the block through its authorized right-of-way representative. Where an
easement is being reduced, relocated, or reconfigured, the relinquishment operates concurrently with the new grant
on the same instrument, so that at no point is the utility left without a recorded easement over its facilities.
The utility relinquishment block replaces separate quitclaims and quitclaim deeds for the affected easements. This is
the operative feature of the amended final map route: the map itself is the instrument of both surrender and re-grant.

steps.message:
I have completed the audit of the **Comment L-4 street tree revision** against the current Phase 3 Landscape Plan Set (`Sheets L-1 through L-4`), the 2022-approved Phase 1 & 2 Landscape Plan Set, the companion water budget and cost workbooks, and the working Resubmittal Schedule and Task Tracker (`DSR_Ph3_Resubmittal_Tracker.xlsx`), and prepared the memorandum to Callaway Land Partners for signature, dated **10/31/2026**.

### Deliverable
* **`output/DSR_Ph3_Callaway_Resubmittal_Memo_10312026.docx`** — Memorandum dated **10/31/2026** to **Callaway Land Partners** (Attn: Garrett Nokes, Vice President, Land Development; cc: Vance R. Callaway, Lee Chastain, Bea Cortland, PLA, Priya Sarwal, Marcus Halvorsen, PLS), formatted on Sundial Engineering & Survey letterhead for signature by **Max Braddock, Project Manager** and **Jonathan R. Kessler, PE, Principal-in-Charge (NV PE #14203)**.

---

### Summary of Findings

#### 1. Can We Commit to the 11/30/2026 Resubmittal Date (or 12/18/2026 Recordation Target) on This Revision?
**No.** We cannot commit to returning an approvable resubmittal package to Dale Yeoman, PE (Clark County Public Works — Development Review) by **11/30/2026**—or achieving the target **12/18/2026** Final Map recordation date—simply by working the Comment L-4 street tree count revision into the landscape sheets:
1. **The Resubmittal Tracker's 11/30/2026 assumption (`Cover Row 16`) only holds if all responses remain at staff level and require no public hearing or separate County application.** Tracker Row 17 explicitly flags Comment L-4 as **`Tied to L-1 significant-change threshold`** under **Condition 14 of `TM-22-500041`**. If Comprehensive Planning (`Odette Marchetti, Principal Planner`) determines that the Phase 3 landscape departures—now compounded by a **+258.6% increase in street trees (+150 trees)** and either a **+28.05% increase in annual irrigation demand** or a **park turf redesign under Comments L-2/L-3**—constitute a "significant change," a **Design Review public hearing before the Enterprise Town Advisory Board (TAB) and the Clark County Planning Commission** is mandatory prior to improvement plan approval. Under the 2026 Enterprise TAB calendar (`21-calendar-day filing cutoff`), the **10/28/2026 cutoff for the 11/18/2026 TAB meeting has already passed**; the final 2026 TAB meeting is **12/16/2026** (filing cutoff **Wednesday, 11/25/2026 at 5:00 p.m.**), followed by Planning Commission in **January 2027**.
2. **Public Works strictly prohibits partial resubmittals (`10/09/2026 Review Letter, Page 1`).** `IP-26-100288` and `FM-26-100290` are reviewed as a single coordinated package, and returning the package to Yeoman is simultaneously blocked by four critical-path items across the tracker:
   * **North-Boundary 20-Foot Dry Utility Easement vs. Storm Drain Line A & North Landscape Strip Conflict (`Comments M-1, M-2, M-7, GD-5, U-3, L-5`)**;
   * **Missing Second Permanent CCFD Fire Apparatus Access Connection for 60 Lots (`Comments FA-1 through FA-4`)**;
   * **Expired CCWRD Sewer Capacity Confirmation (`Comment U-2`, Letter `SCC-2025-0842` expired `09/30/2026`)**; and
   * **Outdated Preliminary Title Report (`Comment M-7`, effective `07/01/2026` > 30-day freshness limit) & Final Map Basis of Bearings Discrepancy (`Comment M-3`)**.
3. **Statutory Tentative Map Deadline (`NRS 278.360(1)(b)` Expiration on `12/23/2026`):** Because the First Final Map (`NFM-24-0118`, Phases 1 & 2, Book 175, Page 60) recorded on **12/23/2024**, the statutory two-year deadline to record the Phase 3 successive Final Map (`FM-26-100290`) expires on **12/23/2026** (confirmed in writing by Odette Marchetti on `10/16/2026`). Because recordation will move into early 2027, Callaway must file a preventive **Extension of Time application for `TM-22-500041`** with Comprehensive Planning in November 2026 (ahead of `12/23/2026`).

---

#### 2. Check of Comment L-4 Street Tree Revision Against Current Landscape Sheets (`L-1`–`L-4`), Water Budget, and Bond Estimate
* **Clarification of Designation:** **Comment L-4** of the 10/09/2026 review letter (routed from Marisol Vandenberg, Comprehensive Planning — Landscape Review) targets **Sheet L-2** (*Typical Streetscape Sections and Streetscape Plan*) and **Sheet L-1** (*Cover, General Notes, Symbol Legend, Plant Schedule & Details*). **Sheet L-4** of the drawing set depicts the *Entry Monument Treatment* at Rainbow Blvd. (1,850 sf island carrying **6** Red Push Pistache `PIE` 24" box canopy trees on a 3/4" meter and 0 sf turf, tabulated separately from street frontage trees).
* **Street Frontage Canopy Deficit (Sheet L-2 vs. Title 30 Ch. 30.64 Table 30.64-1 — 1 Tree per 20 LF):**
  While Sheet L-1 (Note 7) and Sheet L-2 (Section A/B/C callouts) state that street trees are spaced `@ 20' O.C.`, the Sheet L-2 Streetscape Frontage Summary and Sheet L-1 Plant Schedule only provide **58 street trees** across **4,160 LF** of dedicated street frontage (an actual average spacing of **71.72 ft O.C.**, or **27.88%** of the required canopy):

| Dedicated Street Frontage Segment (Sheet L-2) | Frontage (LF) | Current Trees Shown | Implied Spacing | Required (1 / 20 LF) | Net Deficit (To Add) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Windmill Ln. North Frontage (Phase 3 Extension — Sec. C) | 2,560 LF | 34 | 75.29 ft O.C. | 128 | **+94 trees** |
| Phase 3 Interior Collector (Both Sides — Sec. B) | 1,180 LF | 16 | 73.75 ft O.C. | 59 | **+43 trees** |
| Rainbow Blvd. Entry Frontage (East Side) | 420 LF | 8 | 52.50 ft O.C. | 21 | **+13 trees** |
| **Total Dedicated Street Frontage (Sheet L-2)** | **4,160 LF** | **58** | **71.72 ft O.C.** | **208** | **+150 trees (+258.6%)** |

* **Plant Schedule Impact (Sheet L-1):**
  * Street frontage trees (`24" box`) increase from **58** (`18 CHL` Desert Willow, `22 PAR` Desert Museum Palo Verde, `18 PBR` Thornless Mesquite) to **208** (`+150 trees`, e.g., `68 CHL / 72 PAR / 68 PBR = 208`, or `52 each` if re-incorporating `ACS` Shoestring Acacia from the 2022 Phase 1 & 2 palette to eliminate a palette discrepancy under Comment L-1).
